newsitem.title: USA: Woolworth to close 5-and-10 stores, ending an era.
newsitem.headline: Woolworth to close 5-and-10 stores, ending an era.

text.p: Woolworth Corp. said Thursday it will close all 400 of its five-and-dime stores in the United States, abandoning the low-priced general merchandise business that has been its trademark for 118 years.

The retailer said it will take a charge of about $223 million to convert about 100 of the stores in prime locations to Foot Locker shoe stores, Champs Sports stores or other speciality formats. It will close or sell the remaining stores and a distribution centre in Denver, Pa.
Woolworth also said it plans to change its corporate name later this year to better reflect its speciality store chains, which also include the Northern Group of clothing stores.

"We made the very difficult decision to close our domestic F.W. Woolworth general merchandise operations to help assure the continuing profitable growth of the Woolworth Corp. and to better serve all of our constituencies," Chairman Roger Farah said in a statement.

The company, named for founder Frank W. Woolworth, said the decision ends a long attempt to squeeze profits from a business that accounts for about $1 billion of the New York-based retailer's annual sales, which exceed $8 billion.
The move also ends an effort to bring the business, which began in 1879, into retailing's modern age, it said.

"Despite our best efforts and the hard work of the F.W. Woolworth team, the business continued to lose money and it became clear that F.W. Woolworth would be unable, in the foreseeable future, to return to profitability as well as meet our minimum performance standards," Farah said.

Employees shed tears but investors welcomed the news and Woolworth stock jumped $2.56 to $27.625 in consolidated morning on the New York Stock Exchange. Woolworth said the restructuring would help its results over the next two years.
In Chicago, long-time employees expressed great sadness over the news. "It's so sad," said Dorine, a 20-year employee who has worked at Woolworth stores since she was 18.
"I just left a store they closed two years ago," she said from behind a food counter. "It's almost like a family," she said, fighting back tears.

The F.W. Woolworth division lost $24 million on $224 million in sales in the quarter ended on April 26. In 1996, the division generated sales of about $1 billion and an operating loss before one-time items of $37 million.

The unit operates general merchandise stores in 35 states, Puerto Rico and the U.S. Virgin Islands, and has about 3,600 full-time and 5,600 part-time employees. Woolworth said it will provide the workers with severance pay and outplacement counselling.
The charge for discontinued operations, equal to $1.66 a share, will be taken in the second quarter to pay for ending leases, severance, inventory liquidation and other expenses.
It plans to close the stores in coming months, slashing prices on merchandise and selling fixtures, including display cases, soda fountain items, signage and furniture, as well.

Woolworth operates 7,558 stores in North America, Europe, Australia and Asia, including Foot Locker, Northern Reflections, After Thoughts and Champs Sports. The company also operates general merchandise stores in Germany, Mexico and Canada.
